name: Summon a Creature from Elsewhere on Earth
summary: Pull a living creature from some other place in the physical world to your summoning spot. A tiny one, house-cat size or smaller, needs far less power.
system: Takes 2 to 10 successes, more for big creatures and long distances. Nearly always vulgar; the Storyteller may allow exceptions.

optional.purpose: win the creature over to your side right away
sway the creature to your side right away

source.section: Summoning, Binding, Bargaining, and Warding: The Basics
Summoning, Binding, Bargaining, and Warding: The Basics

name: Summon a Spirit Through the Gauntlet
summary: Call out to a spirit, then drag it across the Gauntlet into the material world; with more rank you can bring a whole group over. What arrives still has to be bargained with.
system: A nature spirit in its own element is easy: open the Gauntlet and let it through. A major entity has to be fetched from its home Realm for 10 to 15 successes or more. Bargaining: if you score no successes on a roll, the spirit may roll Willpower (difficulty your Spirit rank +5) to leave or attack; the Pact is a resisted Willpower contest where each side needs successes equal to the other's Willpower. Quintessence offered to a spirit becomes Essence point for point.

Summoning, Binding, Bargaining, and Warding: The Bargaining Process

name: Summon a Ghost Through Its Fetter
summary: Call up a particular ghost by working through a Fetter, a thing or place that tied it to its life.

source.section: Summoning, Binding, Bargaining, and Warding: The Basics

name: Summon a Demon, Angel or Other Great Entity
summary: Open a gateway for a mighty being such as an angel or a demon, a big Bygone or a vast alien, and tie it to the material world through an enchanted item, its True Name, or both.
system: Pulling it from its home Realm takes 10 to 15 successes; truly powerful beings from far planes take at least 15, plus 10 more while the Avatar Storm lasts. Needs a prepared space and full protocols, and is vulgar.

source.section: Summoning, Binding, Bargaining, and Warding: The Basics
Summoning, Binding, Bargaining, and Warding: The Basics

name: Give a Summoned Spirit a Flesh Body
summary: Provide a living body for a spirit to move into: grow one from scratch, or evict whatever mind or soul already lives in a body so the spirit can take it over.
system: A near-death experience can also empty a body. The book flags this as very dark magick.

combos.note: drive out the body's owner with Mind
drive out the body's owner with Spirit
drive out the owner with both

source.section: Summoning, Binding, Bargaining, and Warding: The Basics

name: House an Elemental in Its Element
summary: Gather a good amount of an element, like a pool of water or a bonfire, and call up a spirit of that element. It uses its own power to take shape in the material you provided.

source.section: Summoning, Binding, Bargaining, and Warding: The Basics
Summoning, Binding, Bargaining, and Warding: The Basics

name: Build a Golem
summary: Shape material into a body, bind a spirit into it and quicken it with Quintessence: a golem.
system: Spirit binds the entity, Matter forms the body, Prime animates it. Every 2 successes give the golem 1 Durability and 1 Structure (M20 pp. 439-440); if attacks bring those to zero it breaks apart and the spirit goes free.

source.section: Summoning, Binding, Bargaining, and Warding: The Basics

name: Ward Against Elemental Energies
summary: Bar a kind of energy, such as fire, electricity, light or sound, at a threshold or a surface. The same ward can make a doorway airtight, which matters next to a vacuum.
system: Intense radiation and nuclear forces need Forces 5, and so Correspondence 5, since Correspondence must be at least your highest other Sphere in the ward; shutting out a nuclear blast takes Matter 5 too. Price: 1 Quintessence for the ward plus 1 per objective, and each objective adds 1 to the successes needed. Successes set how long it holds: 1 a turn, 2 a scene, 3 a day, 4 a story, 5 six months; permanent takes 10 plus 1 per objective and 1 more Quintessence per Sphere. As a major ward it costs 1 extra Quintessence per Sphere (2 per Sphere if permanent). Paradox: 1 point per dot of the highest Sphere, +1 if someone watched, added to your wheel without a backlash unless you botch.

optional.purpose: make the seal watertight as well

coincidentalIf: Set up inside a Sanctum or Realm that is built around your own magick.

name: Ward Against Substances and Objects
summary: Keep a kind of material thing out: a plain substance like steel or glass, a complex object like a gun or car, or advanced artificial things like robots and computers.
system: Price: 1 Quintessence for the ward plus 1 per objective, and each objective adds 1 to the successes needed. Successes set how long it holds: 1 a turn, 2 a scene, 3 a day, 4 a story, 5 six months; permanent takes 10 plus 1 per objective and 1 more Quintessence per Sphere. As a major ward it costs 1 extra Quintessence per Sphere (2 per Sphere if permanent). Paradox: 1 point per dot of the highest Sphere, +1 if someone watched, added to your wheel without a backlash unless you botch.

combos.note: simple uniform substances: steel, glass, marble, water

coincidentalIf: Set up inside a Sanctum or Realm that is built around your own magick.

name: Ward Against Primium
summary: A Tradition ward against the Technocracy's anti-magick metal Primium. It does not hold perfectly, but it slows down an invading force.
system: Can be broken like any ward (see Unweave a Ward).
coincidentalIf: Set up inside a Sanctum or Realm that is built around your own magick.

source.section: Summoning, Binding, Bargaining, and Warding: Warding

name: Ward Against a Resonance or Synergy
summary: Turn back a particular flavor of Resonance or Synergy at the threshold, for example a holy ward that stops Infernal essence. An optional rule, since it gets complicated quickly.
system: Resonance and Synergy are detailed in The Book of Secrets, Chapter Two.
coincidentalIf: Set up inside a Sanctum or Realm that is built around your own magick.

source.section: Summoning, Binding, Bargaining, and Warding: Warding

name: Lock a Ward into an Object, Element or Creature
summary: Build a ward into the Pattern of the thing that carries it: floorboards, a door, a gadget, a fire, or a living being. With Prime it becomes a traveling ward that goes where the thing goes, and nothing it bars can touch that thing.
system: Air, light, heat and radiation are too thin to hold a ward, though shadows oddly can. A traveling ward costs 1 more Quintessence and pushes barred things off its surface instead of stopping them at a line; it only covers what it sits on, so a warded jacket leaves your legs open. Every 3 extra successes push the barrier one more yard out (the cost chart lists 3 Quintessence per yard). Pressing your own warded thing into what it bars cancels the ward for you, but not when someone else does it. Correspondence must match the highest other Sphere, so Forces 5 needs Correspondence 5.

combos.note: fire, electricity, or gadgets that use them
a vast area of an element (the largest need Forces 5)
an item, substance or building material
complex objects such as computers or cars
a living being, so it travels with them

optional.purpose: the ward travels with the thing until its Duration runs out (+1 Quintessence)
a permanent traveling ward, which makes the thing a Wonder

coincidentalIf: Set up inside a Sanctum or Realm that is built around your own magick.

name: Circumstantial Ward (Triggered by an Event)
summary: Set a ward that stays dormant until a named event happens, such as a certain person opening a door or a particular ghost showing up, then springs into place.
system: Works only once, but waits as long as it takes. Costs just 1 Quintessence plus 1 per objective.

combos.note: plus the Spheres for what the ward bars

source.section: Summoning, Binding, Bargaining, and Warding: Warding

name: Dante's Laptop: Ward a Device Against a Group of People
summary: Worked example: ward a laptop so Black Suits cannot get hold of it. Forces and Matter tie the ward into the machine's power and parts, Life and Mind pick Black Suits out from everyone else, and Prime invests it.
system: At least 2 successes ward it for a turn; more buy longer. Temporary: 2 Quintessence (ward and objective), plus 1 because it travels. Permanent with Prime 4: 6 Quintessence in all. Other major wards can be built on top of this frame.

optional.purpose: make the ward permanent

coincidentalIf: Set up inside a Sanctum or Realm that is built around your own magick.

source.section: Summoning, Binding, Bargaining, and Warding: Dante's Laptop

name: Minor Ward Against Living Things or Spirits
summary: A basic summoner's precaution. The ward does not block or hurt its target, but it hampers anything the target tries to do to you.
system: Costs 1 Quintessence plus 1 per objective. For the Duration, each success takes one success off the target's actions against you. Usually laid on a pentacle, a circle or a room's entrances. Carried versions can have side effects that clash with a spirit's bargain.

optional.purpose: put it on jewelry or clothing you wear

source.section: Summoning, Binding, Bargaining, and Warding: Minor Wards
Summoning, Binding, Bargaining, and Warding: Minor Wards

name: Minor Area Ward: Keep Out or Stay In
summary: Put a place under a gentle push that tells outsiders to stay away, or tells those inside to stay put. Nothing is actually blocked, but crossing feels wrong.
system: Each success takes one success off an intruder's rolls inside the area. The NWO uses it to shoo away the curious.

optional.purpose: tilt probability inside the area
deter living things
deter non-living intruders
discourage Umbral intrusion
guard against trespass through time
make the push strong enough to be real mind control

source.section: Summoning, Binding, Bargaining, and Warding: Minor Wards

name: Major Ward: The Ban
summary: The simplest major ward: a kind of creature or spirit, or one named individual, cannot touch you or aim its powers and weapons straight at you.
system: At least 5 successes on a vulgar roll. One named spirit needs its True Name or another link (a Fetter, a sigil, a tied object); one particular mortal needs an item from their life plus Mind 4. It does not stop indirect attacks through other people or things, and it drops if you botch a Contest of Wills. As a major ward it costs 1 extra Quintessence per Sphere (2 per Sphere if permanent). Paradox: 1 point per dot of the highest Sphere, +1 if someone watched, added to your wheel without a backlash unless you botch.

combos.note: one specific creature, with a sample of its Pattern
a type of people, or one particular person

optional.purpose: invest the ward with Prime 4 instead of 2, as for a permanent ward

source.section: Summoning, Binding, Bargaining, and Warding: Warding
Summoning, Binding, Bargaining, and Warding: The Ban

name: Major Ward: Binding and the Gauntlet Cage
summary: Lock a spirit inside a warded space, or shut it out. The cage version hardens the Gauntlet in the area to 10; the binding version holds the spirit there until you let go or the Duration ends.
system: Against an unwilling spirit you roll the Effect at difficulty equal to its Willpower while the Storyteller rolls its Willpower at difficulty equal to yours; win and it is held, tie and both roll again. Each success takes one off its attempts to break out. Uses: imprison it, make a Fetish, banish it, drive it out of a possessed host, force it into a body, pin it for wracking.

optional.purpose: trap the spirit inside an object such as a globe or mirror

coincidentalIf: Set up inside a Sanctum or Realm that is built around your own magick.

source.section: Summoning, Binding, Bargaining, and Warding: Binding and the Gauntlet Cage

name: Major Ward: Co-Occupational Ward
summary: A master's version of any ward: the warded thing and what it bars sit on different layers of the same space, so the barred thing passes right through without touching it.
system: Everything else interacts with the warded thing normally. A Black Suit grabbing a co-occupational laptop closes a hand on nothing until the ward is countered. Obviously strange, and vulgar.

combos.note: instead of Correspondence 4, plus the ward's other Spheres

source.section: Summoning, Binding, Bargaining, and Warding: Co-Occupational Wards

name: Major Ward: The Luck Ward
summary: Keep misfortune out of an area, or invite it in, and blunt hostile Entropy magick. Casinos use it against cheating mages; gamblers carry it as a charm.
system: When a non-combat event inside could turn out lucky or unlucky, you roll Arete automatically, with no action needed. The Storyteller decides which events count. One use per Quintessence spent on the ward; more uses cost 1 Quintessence each. Entropy 2 is the minimum; more works too.
coincidentalIf: Set up inside a Sanctum or Realm that is built around your own magick.

source.section: Summoning, Binding, Bargaining, and Warding: Warding
Summoning, Binding, Bargaining, and Warding: The Luck Ward
Summoning, Binding, Bargaining, and Warding: The Luck Ward

name: Psychic Ward: Suggestion of Unease
summary: The ward radiates vague discomfort or a quiet nothing-to-see-here nudge, so most people avoid the place without knowing why.
system: Subtle enough to last as long as the ward stands. Victims may resist with Willpower at difficulty 6 and must beat the successes you rolled for the ward (a permanent ward has at least 10). Lasts the normal Duration unless held with Time 4 or made permanent. See Emotional Surge in the Uncanny Influence section.

optional.purpose: keep the ward going past the normal Duration

coincidentalIf: Set up inside a Sanctum or Realm that is built around your own magick.

name: Psychic Ward: Psychic Pain
summary: Anyone who crosses into the ward gets stabbed by an invisible spike of mental pain. A nastier version shatters the mind and does aggravated harm.
system: Bashing attack on crossing: your Arete is the dice pool, difficulty 6 or the target's Willpower, whichever is higher. Hidden in the ward, so no extra Paradox. One blast per Quintessence spent on the ward. Victims may resist with Willpower at difficulty 6 and must beat the successes you rolled for the ward (a permanent ward has at least 10). Lasts the normal Duration unless held with Time 4 or made permanent.

optional.purpose: keep the ward going past the normal Duration

coincidentalIf: Set up inside a Sanctum or Realm that is built around your own magick.

name: Psychic Ward: Sensory Stunning
summary: Flood trespassers with jumbled sensations until they are stunned, as with Overload, leaving them open for you to strike.
system: One assault per Quintessence spent on the ward. Victims may resist with Willpower at difficulty 6 and must beat the successes you rolled for the ward (a permanent ward has at least 10). Lasts the normal Duration unless held with Time 4 or made permanent.

optional.purpose: keep the ward going past the normal Duration

coincidentalIf: Set up inside a Sanctum or Realm that is built around your own magick.

name: Psychic Ward: Change of Mind
summary: Whoever enters gets a thought, perception or urge you built into the ward: they see an empty room, take a sudden liking to murder, or strip and dance. You set the effect when casting; you cannot steer them live.
system: Built on the Puppetry and Forging Memories Effects from Uncanny Influence. One assault per Quintessence spent on the ward. Victims may resist with Willpower at difficulty 6 and must beat the successes you rolled for the ward (a permanent ward has at least 10). Lasts the normal Duration unless held with Time 4 or made permanent.

optional.purpose: keep the ward going past the normal Duration

name: Psychic Ward: Mind-Barring
summary: Keep particular people out by their mental fingerprint: the ward recognizes them and turns their mind away from going in.
system: Each barred person is a separate objective costing 1 Quintessence. You must have read the person's mind before setting the ward. Spirit 4 (or Dimensional Science) is needed against werecreatures, Umbral entities and other deeply spiritual beings. Victims may resist with Willpower at difficulty 6 and must beat the successes you rolled for the ward (a permanent ward has at least 10). Lasts the normal Duration unless held with Time 4 or made permanent.

optional.purpose: keep the ward going past the normal Duration

coincidentalIf: Set up inside a Sanctum or Realm that is built around your own magick.

name: Psychic Ward: Mood-Barring
summary: Push away anyone in a chosen state of mind, or anyone lacking it: a temple can turn back skeptics, or let in only the reverent.
system: Victims may resist with Willpower at difficulty 6 and must beat the successes you rolled for the ward (a permanent ward has at least 10). Lasts the normal Duration unless held with Time 4 or made permanent.

optional.purpose: work on spiritual as well as mental states
keep the ward going past the normal Duration

name: Major Ward: The Paradigm Ward
summary: Seal a place against followers of chosen paradigms or practices: magick they work through those beliefs counts as vulgar with witnesses on your side of the gate.
system: Each barred paradigm or practice costs 3 more successes and 3 more Quintessence on top of the ward itself (three of them: +9 and +9); they are the objectives, so no separate objective cost. You can bar one form of a practice and allow another at the same price. Optional: mages with lower Arete than yours may lose their Spheres there. Optional pain on entry, 5 Quintessence each: a Psychic Blast, an Entropy assault on their beliefs, or both for 10; one attack per Quintessence invested.
coincidentalIf: Set up inside a Sanctum or Realm that is built around your own magick.

source.section: Summoning, Binding, Bargaining, and Warding: The Paradigm Ward
Summoning, Binding, Bargaining, and Warding: The Paradigm Ward

name: Major Ward: The Time Ward
summary: Split time at a threshold: to someone who crosses, the far side seems frozen, and when they come back they arrive at roughly the moment they left.
system: Time Effects are slippery; the Storyteller may land the traveler in the wrong timestream. See Time Immunity.

source.section: Summoning, Binding, Bargaining, and Warding: Warding
Summoning, Binding, Bargaining, and Warding: The Time Ward

name: Unweave a Ward
summary: Tear down someone else's ward with countermagick. You need at least a dot in every Sphere the ward was built with.
system: Arete roll at difficulty 7 (8 under the Reckoning), spending as much Quintessence as went into the ward. Each success cancels one of the ward's successes and you need one more than it had, so 16 against a 15-success ward. An unwoven ward is gone for good. For a ward of unknown origin the Storyteller picks its Spheres and successes.

combos.note: plus 1 dot in each other Sphere used in the ward

source.section: Summoning, Binding, Bargaining, and Warding: Penetrating a Ward

name: Wrack a Spirit: Spiritual Damage
summary: Hurt a bound or warded spirit to back up your threats. At the lower rank you simply wound it; at mastery you can twist and tear its very form apart.
system: Normal damage, which the spirit heals at its normal rate. Any wracking makes a lasting enemy of the spirit, so it is a last resort.

source.section: Summoning, Binding, Bargaining, and Warding: Wracking the Spirit

name: Wrack a Spirit: Ephemeral Mutation
summary: Reshape a spirit's form the way Life 4 or 5 reshapes a person: painful and humiliating, and dangerous if you make it look like prey for other spirits.
system: Deals the attack's damage on top. Most spirits can reform without much trouble.

source.section: Summoning, Binding, Bargaining, and Warding: Wracking the Spirit

name: Wrack a Spirit: Psychic Agony
summary: Attack a spirit's sense of self, as with Psychic Shatter: agony without injury to its form. Pushed hard enough, it can drive the spirit mad.
system: Works on spirits despite the usual limits on mental attacks against them, because the rites are made for it.

source.section: Summoning, Binding, Bargaining, and Warding: Wracking the Spirit

name: Wrack a Spirit: Primal Disruption
summary: Scramble the Quintessence a spirit is made of. At the lower ranks it is like Rubbing the Bones; at mastery you blast its form apart across the landscape.
system: A disintegrated spirit can heal, but it takes far longer than usual, by Storyteller call.

source.section: Summoning, Binding, Bargaining, and Warding: Wracking the Spirit
Summoning, Binding, Bargaining, and Warding: Wracking the Spirit

name: Wrack a Spirit: Entropic Dispersal
summary: Turn decay on the idea behind a spirit and scatter its conceptual self, for a while or maybe for good.
system: Deals normal damage too. Spirits usually reform in a few months; one with 10 Essence or less never does, while famous beings reform in minutes. Minor spirits scatter at 0 Essence; great ones may need two or three times their Essence in damage. Icons of the human imagination cannot really be dispersed.

source.section: Summoning, Binding, Bargaining, and Warding: Wracking the Spirit

name: Wrack a Spirit: Spiritual Imprisonment
summary: Build a small spirit Realm as a jail, bind the spirit to it and send it away. It stays there until it breaks the Gauntlet Cage, the Realm collapses, or you free it.
system: Can be combined with the other tortures and with Prolonged Agony, which marks the mage as a brute and stains their Resonance.

source.section: Summoning, Binding, Bargaining, and Warding: Wracking the Spirit

name: Wrack a Spirit: Prolonged Agony
summary: Add Time to any spirit wrack: extra actions for more attacks, or a bubble of time where the pain goes on until you stop it or a trigger fires.
system: Spirit 3 is the cheapest wrack to build on; use the Spheres of whichever wrack you choose. This earns enmity that lasts for ages.

combos.note: lock the spirit in a bubble of time
